 Martin Short, Meg Stalter Star In Verizon's Holiday Ads
 by Sarah Mahoney 
 , 
 November 5, 2026
With smartphones high on shoppers’ wish lists this
holiday season, both Verizon and T-Mobile are tossing out plenty of elf bait. For Verizon, that entails actual elves: The carrier has given funny man Martin Short and actors Megan
(“Hacks”) Stalter and Marsai (“Black-ish”) Martin pointy ears, and set them loose in Santa’s workshop.
 “ Holiday Workshop ,” created in-house, takes the overworked trio to the North Pole, where they toss around money snow and talk up the
carrier’s Simplicity plan, offering one line for $30.
 “We set out to build a holiday campaign that people would genuinely smile at, not just scroll past,” said Ricardo
Aspiazu, senior vice president of brand creative, in the announcement. “When you put a comedy titan like Martin Short in a room with comedic dynamos like Meg Stalter and Marsai Martin, you
basically just get out of the way and let the lightning strike.”
 advertisement
 advertisement
 The carrier is also debuting new campaigns for Hispanic audiences. In “Hot Holidays,” Colombian singer and
internet heartthrob Manuel Turizo details Verizon's deals on iPhones. And in “Dos Vidas, Un Destino,” Sebastian Rulli, the Argentine-Mexican actor, stars in his own Verizon-themed
novela. 
 The company is also offering promotional pricing on the latest Apple, Google, Motorola and Samsung phones, with no trade-in needed. Those who opt for a 36-month device payment
plan can get a smartwatch and earbuds.
 T-Mobile, which is promising to give gifting a major upgrade this season, is offering special pricing on  Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 17,
as well as up to $1,200 off the new iPhone Duo. Other deals include $200 off 5G Home Internet.
 Following T-Mobile's new T-Mix plans, customers can choose the benefits they want from a
range of streaming, music, travel, AI assistants, on-demand delivery, and gaming.
 Phones and accessories are likely to be hot gifts this year, according to some surveys: Consumers are feeling
financially strapped, which often makes ultra-practical gifts feel more meaningful. In the Consumer Technology Association’s holiday gift survey, smartphones rank No. 1 on the wish list and
fourth on the gift list, with 53% of respondents considering a phone as a present. (Of those, 63% have their eyes on a foldable or flip model.)
 Phone accessories, including cases, portable
power banks and wireless charging docks, are also high on the list.
